newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian minister calls for cocoa price stability.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian minister calls for cocoa price stability.

text.p: Ivory Coast will seek cocoa price stability in the coming 1996/97 season by trimming output and boosting local processing, its commodities minister said on Wednesday.

"Cocoa markets must have price stability, given a structural surplus of supply over demand," Guy-Alain Gauze told an industry review in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's commercial capital, on the 1995/96 cocoa marketing year which ends next month.
Cocoa prices had been pushed to lows of 650 CFA francs a kilo in April and May because of market and industry speculation over an expected record 1995/96 crop in Ivory Coast, he said.

Gauze, who in September took over as chairman of the International Cocoa Organization council for one year, said world supply in 1996/97 was projected at 2,495,000 tonnes, 208,000 below demand projected at 2,703,000.
Closing stocks were expected to be 1,124,000, he said.
He said Ivory Coast would cut output by 7,000 tonnes as part of International Cocoa Organization plans agreed in September to reduce world output by 15,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
World cuts of 30,000 tonnes in 1997/98 and 45,000 tonnes in 1998/99 would follow, he added.
Ivory Coast's total 1996/97 output was forecast at between 891,000 and 1,009,000 tonnes, he said. Ivory Coast has already set a national output target of 900,000 tonnes for 1996/97.

Production for 1995/96 was heading for a record 1.1 million tonnes against 850,000 tonnes in 1994/95, he said, and price stability was still needed. "Stocks at the end of the 1995/96 season will total 1,275,000 tonnes representing five and a half months of consumption."
The government's decision to process locally in Ivory Coast all or part of the mid-crop had helped boost cocoa prices to around 890-900 CFA francs a kilo, said Gauze.
Ivory Coast has said it plans to increase local processing of cocoa beans to 50 percent of production by the year 2000 to add value and keep prices higher.
Traders say the target was unlikely to be achieved.
London trader ED & F Man in a September report put 1995/96 Ivory Coast grindings at 135,000 tonnes against 108,000 last year.
Cocoa ministers of 12 countries will meet in Gabon on October 21-22 to discuss developments affecting world production as part of an annual Cocoa Producers' Alliance (CPA) meeting.
